title: Potatoes OBrien
description:
Ham is one of our favorite holiday staples, so naturally, when Easter rolled around, we already knew what was going to be the center of attention at our meal that evening.
I have seen a bazillion variations of this recipe on the Internet, but one thing ALWAYS seem consistent with them: cream of something condensed soup. I refuse to use any form of condensed soup in my cooking. Instead:
ingredients: 30-ounce bag frozen hash browns, partially thawed
1 red bell pepper, seeded and chopped
1 green bell pepper, seeded and chopped (optional)
1 sweet or yellow onion, peeled and chopped
1 cup light or fat-free sour cream
1/2-1 tsp. EACH seasoned salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and paprika (to taste)
directions: Preheat oven to 300 degrees F. Spray a 9x13" casserole dish lightly with nonstick cooking spray and set aside.
In a large skillet, melt butter and EVOO. Add chopped onions and bell pepper and saute until slightly softened, 5-7 minutes.
Meanwhile, pour the hash browns in a large bowl, breaking up any pieces that may still be frozen together. Stir in the chopped ham and the cheddar cheese.
In a separate small bowl, combine the sour cream and all seasonings, whisking well.
After the veggies are slightly tender, add them to the large bowl with the hash browns and cheddar cheese. Stir in the sour cream seasoning, mixing well to evenly coat everything.

Press the hash brown mixture evenly into prepared casserole dish, then top with shredded Swiss cheese. Bake at 300 degrees F for 1 hour, or until dish is hot throughout. (If you need this done more quickly, increase the temp to 375 degrees F and bake for 30-40 minutes. Really, it doesn't matter as long as it's hot when you serve it!
